overview: The Xin dynasty was a brief interregnum when Wang Mang attempted radical reforms inspired by ancient Zhou ideals. His utopian policies failed to address real economic problems and natural disasters, leading to widespread rebellion.

items.text: Wang Mang claims the Mandate of Heaven has transferred to him based on omens and classical precedents.
Reforms modeled on the ancient Zhou well-field system and ritual codes.
Private land ownership abolished; all land declared state property to be redistributed equally.
Slavery abolished, though the policy was widely ignored.
Wang Mang's failure discredited radical reform and strengthened conservative Confucianism.
His reign became a cautionary tale about ignoring economic realities for ideological purity.

fall.text: Rebel armies captured Chang'an in 23 CE and killed Wang Mang, ending the Xin dynasty.
